title: BTS Says 'No Thanks' to the Grammys This Year
summary: Imagine winning a big award but deciding you don't even want to try for it. That's what the super famous K-pop group BTS just did! They announced they won't submit their new album, ARIRANG, for the 2027 Grammy Awards. Each member shared the news on their Instagram Stories on July 29. In a statement, BTS said they hope "music can be heard and loved by itself rather than being divided by region or language." That means they don't want their songs to be judged only as "Asian pop" or "K-pop" — they want them to be seen as just great music. BTS has been nominated for five Grammys before. Their first was for the catchy song "Dynamite" in 2020. But some fans think their decision this year is because of a new Grammy category called Best Asian Pop Music Performance. The Grammys added it in June, saying it's for pop music from Asia that uses Asian languages. Some people worry this category might separate Asian artists from the main pop categories, like putting them in a special box instead of letting them compete with everyone else. BTS's new album ARIRANG goes back to a sound that feels more like their early music, with deeper roots in their own style. Member Jin said, "Our most beloved songs are our identity." The group also talked about how cool it was when Bad Bunny performed at the Super Bowl in Spanish and won Album of the Year. Maybe one day, BTS could do something like that too. RM said, "If there's a chance, we definitely want to, some day." For now, they're skipping the Grammys and focusing on making music their own way.
why_it_matters: This story shows that artists sometimes choose to stand up for fairness, even if it means skipping big awards, reminding us that we can speak up about things that matter to us too.

background_read: The Grammy Awards, held every year, are one of the biggest music honors, but they mostly focus on English-language songs and have faced criticism for how they treat music from other languages.
BTS, a seven-member boy band from South Korea, has become one of the world’s most popular groups and has spoken at the United Nations about self-love and following dreams.
Bad Bunny, a Puerto Rican singer who raps and sings in Spanish, showed that music in other languages can win top awards when he performed at the Super Bowl and won Album of the Year.

perspectives.description: BTS's decision shows they value their artistic identity over awards and want their music to be heard without labels.
Some fans are disappointed because the Grammys could have given more recognition to K-pop, and missing out might mean fewer people discover the group.
The Grammy's new category could help Asian artists get noticed, but critics say it might separate them from the main pop competition, keeping music divided.
